# Manifest settings

This page lists every setting of an [application manifest](manifest.md), with
its type, whether it is required or its default, and what it does. It is
generated from the manifest's
[JSON Schema](manifest.md#validation-and-editor-support), so your editor shows
the same descriptions. For how the settings work together, read the
[application manifest](manifest.md) reference and the guides, such as
[serving an application over HTTPS](../networking/routes.md).

Each table's section is headed by the line that starts it in the file, such
as `[[spec.services]]`. Each setting is named by its full TOML path:

- `[]` stands for each entry of an array of tables: `spec.services[].name` is
  the `name` of each `[[spec.services]]`.
- A name in angle brackets, such as `<environment>`, stands for a key you
  choose: `spec.environments.<environment>` is each environment table, such as
  `[spec.environments.staging]`.

A [template](#template) is a string that may reference
[variables](manifest.md#variables), such as `"${{ vars.domain }}"`. Only
settings whose type includes a template accept references. Linked types like
it are described under [value types](#value-types), at the end of the page.

Names, such as those of applications, environments, services, volumes, jobs,
secrets and routes, are 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. They
start with a letter and end with a letter or digit.

## Top level

An application: what it runs, and how its environments and previews deploy it.

### `api_version`

Type: `"piqueld.dev/v1alpha1"`. Required.

Version of the manifest format.

### `kind`

Type: `"Application"`. Required.

Kind of resource the manifest describes.

### `metadata`

Type: table. Required.

The application's identity.

### `spec`

Type: table. Required.

What the application runs, and how it deploys.

## `[metadata]` table

The application's identity.

### `metadata.name`

Type: string. Required.

Name of the application. A manifest with another name applies to another application, so rename one with `piquelctl app rename`.

## `[spec]` table

What the application runs, and how its environments and previews deploy it.

### `spec.environments.<environment>`

Type: table. Optional.

Declares the environment `<environment>` and how it deploys, for at most 64 environments.

### `spec.exports`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Services of this application that other applications may reach, at most 64.

### `spec.imports`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Services of other applications this application reaches, at most 64.

### `spec.jobs`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Containers that run to completion during each deployment, such as database migrations, at most 16. They run in the order listed.

### `spec.manifest`

Type: table. Optional.

The Git repository each deployment reads the manifest from. Without it, deployments use the saved manifest. A manifest read from the repository can't change it: its own `spec.manifest` is ignored.

### `spec.previews`

Type: table. Default: `{ visibility = "private" }`.

Settings shared by every preview.

### `spec.routes`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

HTTP routes to the services, at most 64. They take effect when an environment deploys them.

### `spec.secrets`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Secrets piqueld generates a value for in each environment, at most 64.

### `spec.services`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

The application's services, at most 64.

### `spec.variables.<variable>`

Type: boolean, integer or [template](#template). Optional.

Default value of the variable `<variable>`, referenced as `${{ vars.<variable> }}`. An environment's or the previews' own value replaces it. Variable names start with a letter or `_`, use letters, digits, `_` or `-`, and are at most 63 bytes. Each table of variables holds at most 128.

### `spec.volumes`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Named volumes the services mount, at most 64.

## `[spec.environments.<environment>]` table

Declares an environment and where it deploys from. Without `promote_from`, the environment builds its own manifest: the saved one, or a branch of the `spec.manifest` repository. A block that sets none of `branch`, `commit`, `promote_from` and `sync` leaves an existing environment's source as it is, unless the previous manifest set one of them: removing them returns the environment to the default source.

### `spec.environments.<environment>.branch`

Type: string. Optional.

Branch of the manifest repository the environment deploys. By default, the branch `spec.manifest` names. Needs `spec.manifest`.

### `spec.environments.<environment>.commit`

Type: string. Optional.

Full commit the environment deploys instead of its branch's head. Without `branch`, by default the commit `spec.manifest` pins. Needs `spec.manifest`, and excludes `sync`.

### `spec.environments.<environment>.promote_from`

Type: string. Optional.

Another environment whose releases this one receives with `piquelctl env promote`, instead of building. It excludes `branch`, `commit` and `sync`, and can't lead back to this environment.

### `spec.environments.<environment>.sync`

Type: boolean. Optional.

Whether pushes to the environment's branch deploy it while `spec.manifest.sync` is on. Off when unset. `true` needs `spec.manifest`.

### `spec.environments.<environment>.variables.<variable>`

Type: boolean, integer or [template](#template). Optional.

The environment's value of the variable `<variable>`. It replaces the `[spec.variables]` default, or declares a variable without one.

### `spec.environments.<environment>.visibility`

Type: `"public"` or `"private"`. Default: `"public"`.

The strictest visibility the environment's routes get. `public` restricts nothing; `private` keeps every route on the tailnet.

## `[[spec.exports]]` table

A service of this application that other applications may reach over a private link, as `<service>.<application>`.

### `spec.exports[].applications`

Type: array of strings. Required.

Applications whose environments may import the service: at least one, at most 64, each listed once.

### `spec.exports[].previews`

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Whether previews of those applications may import the service too.

### `spec.exports[].service`

Type: string. Required.

Service of this application to export, at most once.

## `[[spec.imports]]` table

A service of another application this application reaches over a private link, as `<service>.<application>`.

### `spec.imports[].application`

Type: string. Required.

Application exporting the service. It may be this application.

### `spec.imports[].environment`

Type: [template](#template). Optional.

Environment of that application to reach. By default, the one named like the importing environment. It may reference variables, so previews can reach e.g. `staging`.

### `spec.imports[].service`

Type: string. Required.

Service that application exports, imported at most once.

## `[[spec.jobs]]` table

A container that runs to completion during each deployment, such as a database migration.

### `spec.jobs[].command`

Type: array of [templates](#template). Required.

Command the job runs, instead of its service's command and arguments. It can't be empty.

### `spec.jobs[].environment.<name>`

Type: [template](#template). Optional.

The environment variable `<name>` of the job's container only, in addition to its service's. A name the service also sets is an error.

### `spec.jobs[].name`

Type: string. Required.

Name of the job, unique in the application.

### `spec.jobs[].run`

Type: `"before-rollout"`. Required.

When the job runs. `before-rollout` runs it after every source is prepared, before the services roll out.

### `spec.jobs[].secrets`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Secrets only the job's container mounts, in addition to its service's. A target the service already uses is an error.

### `spec.jobs[].service`

Type: string. Required.

Service whose image, environment, secrets, volumes, resource limits and network the job reuses. The job also waits for the service's `depends_on`.

### `spec.jobs[].stop_service`

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Whether the job's service stops before the job runs, once the job's startup dependencies are ready, so its previous version never runs against what the job changes. The service starts again with the rollout, or with the previous deployment if a job fails.

### `spec.jobs[].timeout_seconds`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295. Default: `300`.

Seconds the job may run before the deployment fails, from 1 to 86,400.

### `spec.jobs[].volume_access`

Type: `"read-only"` or `"exclusive"`. Default: `"read-only"`.

How the job mounts its service's volumes. `read-only` mounts every volume read-only, so the job runs beside the services. `exclusive` keeps the writable volumes writable, and stops every service mounting them while the job runs.

## `[[spec.jobs.secrets]]` table

A secret mounted as a file. A name `spec.secrets` declares mounts the environment's generated value; any other name mounts a value from the application's secret store.

### `spec.jobs[].secrets[].name`

Type: [template](#template). Required.

Name of the secret. It may reference variables, so each environment can mount its own stored secret, e.g. `${{ vars.stripe_key }}`.

### `spec.jobs[].secrets[].target`

Type: string. Required.

Absolute path of the file under `/run/secrets/`, unique in the service.

## `[spec.manifest]` table

The Git repository and file each deployment reads the manifest from.

### `spec.manifest.path`

Type: string. Required.

Path of the TOML or JSON manifest file, relative to the repository root.

### `spec.manifest.repository`

Type: table. Required.

The repository holding the manifest, and the branch environments deploy by default.

### `spec.manifest.sync`

Type: table. Default: `{ mode = "off" }`.

Whether pushes to the repository deploy environments and previews.

## `[spec.manifest.repository]` table

A Git repository and the revision to check out. Git uses the host's credentials.

### `spec.manifest.repository.branch`

Type: string. Required.

Branch whose head is checked out when no commit is set.

### `spec.manifest.repository.commit`

Type: string. Optional.

Full commit hash to check out instead of the branch's head.

### `spec.manifest.repository.url`

Type: string. Required.

Clone URL or local path of the repository. It can't contain credentials.

## `[spec.manifest.sync]` table

Whether pushes to the manifest repository deploy. It applies to every preview, and to every environment that opted in and follows a branch without a pinned commit.

### `spec.manifest.sync.mode`

Type: `"off"`, `"poll"` or `"webhook"`. Required.

- `"off"`: Deploy only when asked.
- `"poll"`: List the repository's branch heads every `interval_seconds`.
- `"webhook"`: List the branch heads when GitHub reports a push.

### `spec.manifest.sync.interval_seconds`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295. Only with `mode = "poll"`. Default: `300`.

Seconds between listings, from 60 to 86,400.

## `[spec.previews]` table

Settings shared by every preview.

### `spec.previews.variables.<variable>`

Type: boolean, integer or [template](#template). Optional.

The previews' value of the variable `<variable>`. It replaces the `[spec.variables]` default, or declares a variable without one.

### `spec.previews.visibility`

Type: `"public"` or `"private"`. Default: `"private"`.

The strictest visibility preview routes get. `private` keeps every route on the tailnet; `public` restricts nothing.

## `[[spec.routes]]` table

An HTTP route: requests for a hostname go to a service, or get a redirect. A route sets either `service` and `port`, or `redirect`.

### `spec.routes[].hostname`

Type: [template](#template). Required.

Hostname the route serves, such as `notes.example.com`, unique in the application. A wildcard such as `*.example.com` serves every name one label below `example.com` that no exact route claims.

### `spec.routes[].name`

Type: string. Optional.

Name that selects the route in every environment and preview, e.g. `piquelctl env url --route web`. It is unique in the application and can't reference variables.

### `spec.routes[].port`

Type: integer from 1 to 65535. Optional.

Port the service serves HTTP on, from 1 to 65535. Needs `service`.

### `spec.routes[].redirect`

Type: table. Optional.

Redirect the gateway answers with, instead of a service.

### `spec.routes[].service`

Type: string. Optional.

Service of this application that receives the requests. Needs `port`.

### `spec.routes[].visibility`

Type: `"public"` or `"private"`. Default: `"private"`.

Who may connect: `public` for the internet, or `private` for the tailnet only. The environment's or the previews' visibility can make it stricter, never looser.

## `[spec.routes.redirect]` table

A redirect the gateway answers with.

### `spec.routes[].redirect.preserve_path`

Type: boolean. Default: `true`.

Whether to append the request's path and query to `to`.

### `spec.routes[].redirect.status`

Type: `301`, `302`, `303`, `307` or `308`. Default: `308`.

HTTP status of the redirect.

### `spec.routes[].redirect.to`

Type: [template](#template). Required.

Absolute `http` or `https` URL to redirect to, with a lowercase hostname and no query or fragment. It can't target a hostname the route serves.

## `[[spec.secrets]]` table

A secret whose value piqueld generates for each environment when one of its deployments first needs it. Later deployments and manifest edits keep that value; `piquelctl env secret regenerate` replaces it. A value is never shared with another environment.

### `spec.secrets[].generate`

Type: table. Required.

How piqueld generates the value.

### `spec.secrets[].name`

Type: string. Required.

Name of the secret, unique in the application. It can't reference variables.

## `[spec.secrets.generate]` table

How piqueld generates a secret's value.

### `spec.secrets[].generate.type`

Type: `"random"` or `"rsa"`. Required.

- `"random"`: Random bytes from the operating system, encoded as text.
- `"rsa"`: An RSA private key, in PKCS#8 PEM.

### `spec.secrets[].generate.bits`

Type: integer of at most 65535. Required with `type = "rsa"`.

Size of the key in bits: 2048, 3072 or 4096.

### `spec.secrets[].generate.bytes`

Type: integer of at most 65535. Required with `type = "random"`.

Number of random bytes before encoding, from 16 to 512.

### `spec.secrets[].generate.encoding`

Type: `"hex"` or `"base64url"`. Only with `type = "random"`. Default: `"hex"`.

Text encoding of the bytes: lowercase `hex`, or unpadded `base64url`.

## `[[spec.services]]` table

A service: containers running one image, kept at their replica count.

### `spec.services[].arguments`

Type: array of [templates](#template). Optional.

Arguments that replace the image's default arguments, at most 128 elements of 4,096 bytes each.

### `spec.services[].command`

Type: array of [templates](#template). Optional.

Command that replaces the image's entrypoint, at most 128 elements of 4,096 bytes each. When empty, the image's entrypoint runs.

### `spec.services[].depends_on`

Type: array of strings. Optional.

Services of this application that must be running and healthy before this one rolls out, each listed once.

### `spec.services[].environment.<name>`

Type: [template](#template). Optional.

The environment variable `<name>` of the service's containers. Names use letters, digits and `_`, don't start with a digit, and are at most 255 bytes. Values are at most 65,536 bytes. At most 256 variables; `PIQUELD_INGRESS_PROXIES` is reserved.

### `spec.services[].files`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Read-only files mounted into the containers, at most 32. Their contents are never rendered with variables. An application's files total at most 2 MiB.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck`

Type: table. Optional.

How Docker checks that a container is healthy. Rollouts and the services depending on this one wait until it passes.

### `spec.services[].mounts`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Volumes mounted into the containers, at most 32.

### `spec.services[].name`

Type: string. Required.

Name of the service, unique in the application. The application's other services reach it by this name.

### `spec.services[].receives_telemetry`

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Whether the service receives the daemon's traces, metrics and logs, on a socket in `/run/piqueld/telemetry`, once its environment is granted telemetry. At most one service of an application receives telemetry, with one replica.

### `spec.services[].replicas`

Type: integer of at most 65535 or [typed template](#typed-template). Default: `1`.

Number of containers, from 1 to 100.

### `spec.services[].resources`

Type: table. Optional.

CPU and memory limits of each container.

### `spec.services[].rollout`

Type: table. Optional.

How Docker replaces the service's containers on each deployment.

### `spec.services[].secrets`

Type: array of tables. Optional.

Secrets mounted as files, at most 64.

### `spec.services[].source`

Type: table. Required.

Where the service's image comes from: a prebuilt image, or a Git build.

## `[[spec.services.files]]` table

A read-only file mounted into a service's containers, from exactly one source: `path` in the manifest's repository, or inline `content`. Its content can't be empty, and is at most 500 KiB.

### `spec.services[].files[].content`

Type: string. Required unless `path` is set.

The file's content, inline.

### `spec.services[].files[].mode`

Type: [file mode](#file-mode). Default: `"0444"`.

Octal permissions, from `"0000"` to `"0777"`. The file is owned by root.

### `spec.services[].files[].path`

Type: string. Required unless `content` is set.

Path of a UTF-8 text file in the manifest's repository, relative to its root, read at the commit the manifest was read from. Only repository-backed applications can use it.

### `spec.services[].files[].target`

Type: string. Required.

Absolute path of the file in the container, unique among the service's mount, secret and file targets. It can't be in `/run/secrets` or `/run/piqueld`.

## `[spec.services.healthcheck]` table

How Docker checks that a service's containers are healthy.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.type`

Type: `"http"` or `"command"`. Required.

- `"http"`: Send an HTTP `GET` to a port of the container. A 2xx or 3xx status passes. The image needs nothing for it.
- `"command"`: Run a command in the container, without a shell. Exit code 0 passes.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.command`

Type: array of [templates](#template). Required with `type = "command"`.

Command and arguments to run. It can't be empty.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.interval_seconds`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295 or [typed template](#typed-template). Default: `10`.

Seconds between checks, from 1 to 3,600.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.path`

Type: [template](#template). Only with `type = "http"`. Default: `"/health"`.

Absolute HTTP path to request.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.port`

Type: integer of at most 65535 or [typed template](#typed-template). Required with `type = "http"`.

Container port to request, from 1 to 65535.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.retries`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295 or [typed template](#typed-template). Default: `3`.

Consecutive failed checks that make a container unhealthy, from 1 to 100.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.start_period_seconds`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295 or [typed template](#typed-template). Default: `0`.

Seconds after a container starts during which failed checks don't count, up to 3,600.

### `spec.services[].healthcheck.timeout_seconds`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295 or [typed template](#typed-template). Default: `3`.

Seconds a check may take before it fails, from 1 to the interval.

## `[[spec.services.mounts]]` table

A volume mounted into a service's containers.

### `spec.services[].mounts[].read_only`

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Whether the containers mount the volume read-only. A writable mount makes rollouts stop the old container before starting its replacement.

### `spec.services[].mounts[].target`

Type: string. Required.

Absolute path of the mount in the container, unique in the service. It can't be `/run/piqueld/probe` or `/run/piqueld/telemetry`, or a path inside them.

### `spec.services[].mounts[].volume`

Type: string. Required.

Name of a volume in `spec.volumes`.

## `[spec.services.resources]` table

CPU and memory limits of each of a service's containers. Set at least one.

### `spec.services[].resources.cpu_millis`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295 or [typed template](#typed-template). Optional.

CPU limit in thousandths of a CPU, from 1 to 1,048,576: `500` is half a CPU.

### `spec.services[].resources.memory_bytes`

Type: integer of at most 18446744073709551615 or [typed template](#typed-template). Optional.

Memory limit in bytes, from 1 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807.

## `[spec.services.rollout]` table

How Docker replaces a service's containers during a deployment, one at a time. An empty block keeps the defaults.

### `spec.services[].rollout.monitor_seconds`

Type: integer of at most 4294967295 or [typed template](#typed-template). Optional.

Seconds Docker watches each new container for failure before it replaces the next one, from 1 to 3,600. 30 when unset.

### `spec.services[].rollout.order`

Type: `"stop-first"`, `"start-first"` or [typed template](#typed-template). Optional.

`stop-first` stops the old container before starting its replacement, with a short downtime. `start-first` starts the replacement first, so both briefly run side by side. When unset, `stop-first` if the service mounts a volume writable or receives telemetry, `start-first` otherwise.

## `[[spec.services.secrets]]` table

A secret mounted as a file. A name `spec.secrets` declares mounts the environment's generated value; any other name mounts a value from the application's secret store.

### `spec.services[].secrets[].name`

Type: [template](#template). Required.

Name of the secret. It may reference variables, so each environment can mount its own stored secret, e.g. `${{ vars.stripe_key }}`.

### `spec.services[].secrets[].target`

Type: string. Required.

Absolute path of the file under `/run/secrets/`, unique in the service.

## `[spec.services.source]` table

Where a service's image comes from.

### `spec.services[].source.type`

Type: `"image"` or `"git"`. Required.

- `"image"`: Pull a prebuilt image from a registry.
- `"git"`: Build the image from a Git repository.

### `spec.services[].source.build`

Type: table. Required with `type = "git"`.

How to build the image.

### `spec.services[].source.image`

Type: [template](#template). Required with `type = "image"`.

Image reference, such as `ghcr.io/example/notes:1.4.0`, with an optional tag or digest. It can't contain a URL scheme or credentials.

### `spec.services[].source.repository`

Type: `"self"` or table. Required with `type = "git"`.

Repository to build: `"self"` for the manifest's own repository, at the commit the manifest was read from, or a table naming another one. `"self"` needs `spec.manifest`.

## `[spec.services.source.build]` table

How to build a Git source's image.

### `spec.services[].source.build.type`

Type: `"docker"`. Required.

- `"docker"`: Build the image with Docker Buildx, from a Dockerfile.

### `spec.services[].source.build.args.<name>`

Type: [template](#template). Optional.

The value of the build argument `<name>`, passed with `--build-arg`. Docker records it in the image's metadata, so pass sensitive values as secrets instead. Build arguments total at most 256 KiB.

### `spec.services[].source.build.context`

Type: [template](#template). Default: `"."`.

Build context directory, relative to the repository root.

### `spec.services[].source.build.dockerfile`

Type: [template](#template). Required.

Path of the Dockerfile, relative to the repository root.

### `spec.services[].source.build.target`

Type: [template](#template). Optional.

Stage of a multi-stage Dockerfile to build. By default, the final stage.

## `[spec.services.source.repository]` table

A Git repository and the revision to check out. Git uses the host's credentials.

### `spec.services[].source.repository.branch`

Type: string. Required.

Branch whose head is checked out when no commit is set.

### `spec.services[].source.repository.commit`

Type: string. Optional.

Full commit hash to check out instead of the branch's head.

### `spec.services[].source.repository.url`

Type: string. Required.

Clone URL or local path of the repository. It can't contain credentials.

## `[[spec.volumes]]` table

A named volume the services mount. Its data is kept across deployments, and when the application is deleted. A preview's volumes are deleted with the preview.

### `spec.volumes[].name`

Type: string. Required.

Name of the volume, unique in the application.

## Value types

### File mode

Type: string.

Octal file permissions from `0000` to `0777`, written as text such as `"0444"` or `"644"`.

### Template

Type: string.

Text that may contain `${{ namespace.name }}` references, with optional whitespace inside the braces. `$${{` writes a literal `${{`; `${VAR}` and `$VAR` are ordinary text, left for shells and applications to expand.

```text
"${{ vars.domain }}"       -> the value of `domain`
"api.${{vars.domain}}"     -> "api." followed by the value of `domain`
"$${{ vars.domain }}"      -> "${{ vars.domain }}", literally
```

### Typed template

Type: string.

A template in a setting of another type, such as an integer: text containing a `${{` reference. A template that is exactly one reference takes the variable's own value, which must have the setting's type; strings are never parsed into numbers. For example, with `replicas = "${{ vars.replicas }}"`, the variable `replicas` must be the integer `2`, not the string `"2"`.
